pros: Guarantees optimal path with admissible heuristic
Dramatically faster than Dijkstra with good heuristic
Explores fewer nodes by focusing search toward goal
Flexible heuristic design for domain-specific optimization
Complete: always finds a path if one exists
Optimal efficiency among informed search algorithms
Easily adaptable to weighted and anytime variants
Widely implemented with extensive optimization techniques
Foundation for modern replanning algorithms (D*, LPA*)
cons: Performance heavily depends on heuristic quality
Poor heuristic can degrade to Dijkstra performance
Memory intensive: stores all explored nodes in open/closed sets
Exponential worst-case complexity with weak heuristic
Requires admissible heuristic — can't always guarantee optimality
Not suitable for dynamically changing graphs without adaptation
Overhead of heuristic computation must be justified
Struggles with very large state spaces (memory-bound)
Bidirectional implementation more complex than unidirectional
Cannot handle negative edge weights without modification
